title: worked/got/went etc. (past simple)
subtitle: I worked / I went
summary: Make the past simple with -ed for regular verbs and learn the most common irregular past forms.

lesson.heading: watch -> watched
lesson.text: Two people are sitting on the sofa in front of the television. They **watch** television every evening (present simple). They **watched** television yesterday evening (past simple). **watched** is the past simple.

lesson.heading: The form is the same for everybody
lesson.note: There is no extra -s for he/she/it in the past simple.

lesson.heading: Regular verbs: + -ed
lesson.text: Most verbs are *regular*. The past simple ends in **-ed**: work -> **worked**, clean -> **cleaned**, start -> **started**, dance -> **danced**, stay -> **stayed**, need -> **needed**.

examples.text: I clean my teeth every morning. This morning I **cleaned** my teeth.
Terry **worked** in a bank from 1996 to 2003.
Yesterday it **rained** all morning. It **stopped** at lunchtime.
We **enjoyed** the party last night. We **danced** a lot and **talked** to a lot of people.

lesson.heading: Spelling
rows: work -> worked, clean -> cleaned, stay -> stayed
try -> tried, study -> studied, copy -> copied

lesson.heading: Irregular verbs
lesson.text: Some verbs are *irregular*. Their past simple does **not** end in -ed, so you have to learn each one.

examples.text: I usually get up early, but this morning I **got** up at 9 o'clock.
We **did** a lot of work yesterday.
Caroline **went** to the cinema three times last week.
James **came** into the room, **took** off his coat and **sat** down.

lesson.heading: Important irregular verbs
lesson.note: put and read do not change: put -> put, read -> read (the past is pronounced 'red').

lesson.text: Learn each irregular verb in a short sentence, not on its own: *Yesterday I went to work by car.*

exercises.prompt: I clean my teeth every morning. This morning I ___ my teeth.
It was hot in the room, so I ___ the window.
Match each verb with its past simple.
The film was very long. It started at 7.15 and ___ at 10 o'clock.
We often go to the cinema at weekends. Last Sunday we ___ to the cinema.
Is the past simple of this verb regular (-ed) or irregular?
It's a nice day today, but yesterday it ___ all day.
When I was a child, I ___ to be a doctor.

exercises.statement: Kate meets her friends every evening. She meeted her friends yesterday evening.
exercises.explanation: She met her friends yesterday evening. meet is irregular: meet -> met.

exercises.prompt: Rachel often loses her keys. She ___ her keys last week.
Last Tuesday Lisa ___ from London to Madrid.
Put the words in the right order to tell the story: (took off his coat / came into the room / James / and sat down)
exercises.answer: James came into the room, took off his coat and sat down.
exercises.explanation: Three irregular past simple verbs in one sentence: came, took, sat.
